I have resolved the issue by ensuring the base table alias is initialized via [`self.query.get_initial_alias()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-2ffcgl1r/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1409-L1412) in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-2ffcgl1r/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1412) in [compiler.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-2ffcgl1r/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py).

Previously, an unfiltered `Model.objects.all().delete()` had an empty `alias_map` when checking `single_alias`, causing `single_alias` to evaluate to `False` (`0 == 1`) and fall back to a `WHERE id IN (SELECT ...)` subquery instead of a direct `DELETE FROM` statement.
